storage: fix SPENT_UTXOS_TABLE double-open in commit_reorg_atomic
Contributed by Ziyang (as exfer-stack) upstream to ahuman-exfer/exfer, the Exfer chain itself.
This pull request is merged.
https://github.com/ahuman-exfer/exfer/pull/14

**Draft** — opening early so the fix is visible while live IBD catch-up on `exfer-node-stack` is still mid-flight. Will mark ready once I observe the patched binary land a real reorg on fly without erroring.

## The bug

`commit_reorg_atomic` opens `SPENT_UTXOS_TABLE` twice within one `write_txn`:

* once near the top (\`storage.rs:1155\`) for the new-chain write phase — \`spent_table.insert(...)\` for each new_chain_spent row;
* once again inside the orphan-undo inner block (\`storage.rs:1254\`) for the spent-UTXO restore reads.

redb forbids opening the same table twice in one txn and returns:

\`\`\`
Db(TableAlreadyOpen("spent_utxos", Location { file: "src/chain/storage.rs", line: 1155, column: 45 }))
\`\`\`

The inner-block open runs unconditionally (before the \`for orphan in old_chain_blocks\` body), so every single call to \`commit_reorg_atomic\` errored — even when \`old_chain_blocks\` is empty.

## How it surfaced

\`commit_reorg_atomic\` has no direct unit tests in \`src/chain/storage.rs\`'s test module, and the only caller (\`sync.rs:2840\`) needs an actual fork in the live header stream to fire. PR #13 (wedge-fallback IBD candidate selection) merged conceptually first: once that fix unwedged the supervisor and IBD started actually streaming blocks past h=605,666 on \`exfer-node-stack\`, the first fork point hit \`commit_reorg_atomic\` and crashed in a tight retry loop:

\`\`\`
14:01:45  Reorg: undoing 1 blocks, applying 2 blocks
14:01:45  Sync manager: IBD failed: IBD block processing failed:
            storage error: Table 'spent_utxos' already opened at:
            src/chain/storage.rs:1155:45
14:01:45  Sync manager: starting IBD from identity [...]
            → loop forever, no tip progress
\`\`\`

## The fix

Minimal, structural:

\`\`\`rust
{
    let mut utxos = write_txn.open_table(UTXOS_TABLE)?;
-   let spent_table = write_txn.open_table(SPENT_UTXOS_TABLE)?;
    for orphan in old_chain_blocks {
        ...
        if let Some(spent_guard) = spent_table.get(orphan_id.as_bytes().as_ref())? {
            ...
        }
    }
-   drop(spent_table);
    drop(utxos);
}
\`\`\`

The outer \`spent_table\` declared at the top of the function (\`storage.rs:1155\`) is owned by the surrounding scope and lives until the end of the outer block; the orphan-undo loop reads through that handle. Removing the \`drop(spent_table)\` is required because the outer handle must remain valid for the rest of the outer scope.

No semantic change to redb-on-disk layout or to the operations performed — same writes in the same order to the same tables, just one handle instead of two.

## Tests

Two regression tests added in \`chain::storage::tests\`:

1. **\`commit_reorg_atomic_does_not_double_open_spent_utxos_table\`** — minimal repro with empty \`old_chain_blocks\`. Pre-fix this still errors because the second open runs unconditionally.
